title: AeroZard team guide and notes
content: This post is to practise writing and posting these blog-like logs. It’s also to try log and get down my current knowledge of Pokemon VGC and my current understanding of the game with the current team I’ve been using for a month or so now.  To get this out the way, let’s go through the line against Louis Fontvielle’s regional-winning rain team:  flowchart TD     A["Opp leads: Basculegion + Raichu X"] --> B["Our lead: Garchomp + Farigiraf<br/>Back: Charizard + Sylveon"]     B --> C["Turn 1:<br/>Garchomp switches to Sylveon<br/>Farigiraf uses Thunderbolt on Basculegion"]     C --> D{"Did they switch in Pelipper?"}     D -- Yes --> E["Farigiraf: Thunderbolt Pelipper<br/>Sylveon: Protect"]     D -- No --> F["Sylveon: Protect<br/>Farigiraf: Trick Room"]

title: Trying to apply search algorithms to soil mechanics related applications
tags: soil mechanics, geotechnical, ground engineering, neural networks
content: Recently, there have been advances in AI for a game I play often, which may change the way the community has to play the game, with irreversible consequences. While I will keep my personal feelings about that situation out of this post, it did start to get me to think: “Can these methods of learning be applied to testing in soil conditions?”. More specifically for piles in offshore wind farms, as it was something I had previously been interested in and have looked into.  The purpose of this project is to understand and see whether the concepts used in the game that I play can be applied in a similar way to the installation of cluster piles for offshore wind foundations in sand.  Currently unfinished, will update the post with more content incrementally as I learn more. I also must keep up with my studies but I’ll try to get something on here soon
